meta.title: Lily's Weather Diary
meta.textType: functional: a weather diary for one week

paragraphs: Teacher Kim says, "Write the day and the date every morning." My name is Lily, and this week I write the class weather diary. I watch the sky every day. On Monday, March third, it is sunny. Today it is sunny and hot. I always wear my hat. I drink lots of water, too. On Tuesday, March fourth, it is cloudy. Today it is cloudy, but it is dry. Tom often takes his coat to school.

On Wednesday, March fifth, it rains. Today it is wet. I am dry under my big umbrella. On Thursday, March sixth, a storm comes. The wind is very loud, and the rain is strong. Pip hides under the kitchen table. Tom asks, "Is it a big storm?" I say, "Yes, but we are at home." Pip never likes a storm. On Friday, March seventh, it is windy but sunny. Today the rain stops, and the sun comes out. The whole class is happy.

On Saturday, March eighth, it rains, and then a rainbow comes. The big rainbow is above the school field. Tom and I watch the sky after the rain. Tom thinks it is the best weather. I take a picture of the rainbow. It has red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple. On Sunday, March ninth, I write about the best day of the week. Saturday is the best day because of the rainbow. What is the weather today? Look at the sky and write one sentence. I always look for a rainbow after a storm!
text.summary: Lily writes the class weather diary for one week. She writes the day, the date, and the weather, and she ends the week with a rainbow.
